abstract: Manganese-based single-atom catalysts (SACs) serve as ideal alternatives to expensive Pt-based electrocatalysts for the kinetically sluggish oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in fuel cells, owing to their weak Fenton reaction propensity and potential stability. Nevertheless, enhancing their intrinsic electrochemical activity and site accessibility remains a critical bottleneck for their practical implementation in fuel cells. Herein, a synergistic strategy of chemical etching and phosphorus doping is developed to synthesize atomically dispersed P-doped Mn-N-C materials with a hollow mesoporous structure (H-P-Mn-N-C). Theoretical calculations demonstrate that the as-formed asymmetric MnN3P1 sites reduce the energy barrier of the rate-determining step for OH* desorption and suppress the dissolution of metal centers, thereby endowing the catalyst with fuel cell performance and long-term durability. Specifically, the H-P-Mn-N-C catalyst delivers a peak power density of 745 mW cm-2 in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) and 833 mW cm-2 in anion exchange membrane fuel cells (AEMFCs). Notably, it exhibits only a 17.3% decay after 30,000 square-wave potential cycles in PEMFCs. This work offers a novel perspective for constructing highly active heteroatom-doped non-precious metal catalysts, thereby helping to address the issues of insufficient mass transportation and limited performance in electrocatalytic applications.

title: Induce uniform vertical grain growth via double-site anchoring retards crystallization for perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
abstract: The development of wide bandgap perovskite solar cells (WBG PSCs) holds significant promise for advancing tandem solar cells. However, the intrinsic rapid crystallization kinetics severely impedes the vertical-oriented growth and homogeneous film formation of perovskite crystals, leading to high defect density and compromised device performance. This work proposes an innovative molecular interfacial dual-site anchoring strategy by introducing Sodium 4-Chlorobenzenesulfonate (SCBS) to effectively regulate the perovskite crystallization process. SCBS can coordinate with multiple ions in the perovskite precursors, thereby significantly retarding crystallization kinetics and promoting vertical-oriented and homogeneous grain growth. Moreover, SCBS simultaneously passivates bulk defects and effectively suppresses light-induced halide phase separation. Consequently, the 1.68 eV of WBG PSCs achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.98% and an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.26 V. Furthermore, the unencapsulated optimized devices retained 90% of initial efficiency after 3000 h under a nitrogen atmosphere, showcasing excellent long-term stability. Notably, the monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) achieved a PCE of 32.08%, a VOC of 1.951 V, and a hysteresis index of 0.31%. Therefore, the dual-site anchoring retards crystallization to induce uniform vertical grain growth strategy offers a promising pathway for high-performance and stable PSTSCs.

title: A fully autonomous, wireless dual-mode triboelectric system for broadband vibration monitoring on live 110 kV transmission lines
abstract: Real-time monitoring of aeolian vibrations is critical for the structural health of overhead transmission lines, yet achieving long-term, self-sustained sensing in high-voltage environments remains a persistent challenge. Herein, we report a fully autonomous, wireless vibration monitoring system driven by a dual-mode broadband triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG), which seamlessly integrates broadband energy harvesting, multi-parameter sensing, and wireless transmission. By coupling a freestanding layered structure with mechanical switching strategies and complementary dynamic configurations, the TENG achieves instantaneous discharge (ID) and continuous discharge (CD) modes with distinct sensing functionalities. The ID mode is used for frequency sensing with a response range of 5–88 Hz and an error of <0.5 Hz, while the CD mode enables amplitude sensing with a linear response range of 0.1–4 mm, offering a linearity R2>0.991 and a nonlinear error of δ<3.59%. Beyond the device level, a customized low-loss power management module is developed to boost the charging rate by 7.96 times, successfully driving Bluetooth and infrared communication modules. Significantly, the system was deployed on a live 110 kV transmission line for field testing, demonstrating stable, continuous operation under varying environmental conditions. This work bridges the gap between laboratory-scale TENG innovation and deployable, industrial-relevant high-voltage monitoring systems.

A biobased moisture-electric generator with self-stratified architecture for physiological sensing and energy harvesting
abstract: Wearable, agricultural and environmental sensors increasingly require power sources that operate in humid settings without frequent battery replacement, particularly for skin-mounted patches and remote nodes that are difficult to retrieve. Moisture-enabled electric generators (MEGs) can convert ambient and physiological moisture into electricity, but many systems rely on persistent polymers or complex architectures that complicate scalable, environmentally responsible deployment. Here we report a biodegradable and recyclable MEG fabricated by a single water-based process from food-grade gelatin, sodium chloride and activated carbon. During casting and drying, the composite undergoes self-stratification into an asymmetric layered architecture consisting of a hydrophilic gelatin–salt layer and an activated-carbon layer, sustaining moisture uptake/evaporation cycles that drive directional ion transport and stable output. Single devices deliver open-circuit voltages approaching 1 V and peak current densities up to 1.36 mA cm -2 , maintaining ~1 V output for over one month under controlled conditions. Modular integration scales output to 90 V and 5.08 mA, enabling capacitor charging and low-power demonstrations. Beyond energy harvesting, the films function as self-powered sensors for respiration and speech monitoring, skin-hydration tracking and touchless human–machine interaction. Finally, we demonstrate rapid biodegradation in soil within weeks, and water-based recycling without performance loss, reducing end-of-life burdens for disposable patches and distributed electronics. • A fully biobased MEG platform using only food-grade components, demonstrating that high-performance moisture-powered devices do not need to rely on persistent synthetic polymers or hazardous materials. • The spontaneous formation of an asymmetric layered structure during a single-step water-based casting process represents a scalable fabrication approach that simplifies manufacturing while maintaining device functionality. • Demonstration of simultaneous energy harvesting and physiological sensing capabilities, expanding the utility of MEG technology beyond power generation alone. • Verified dual end-of-life pathways (biodegradation and recycling) that are matched to application contexts, addressing a critical gap in sustainable electronics.

Nanoeffects in the design of catalysts for green energy technologies
abstract: Methane and methanol can serve as CO 2 -neutral energy carriers if they are synthesized through CO or CO 2 hydrogenation with green hydrogen produced using renewable energy sources. In particular, CO x hydrogenation into methanol is conducted on a 100-megaton scale using Cu-ZnO catalysts. The economic attractiveness of CO x hydrogenation can be improved by designing more efficient transition-metal catalysts through atomic-scale understanding of the critical effects of nanostructuring and nanoparticle-support interactions on their properties. Herein, we characterize how coordination numbers of metal atoms, nanoconfinement, and nanoparticle interactions with pristine ZnO support (i.e., nanoeffects) affect computational catalyst design for CO hydrogenation into methanol and methane on transition metals, such as Ir, Pd, Pt, Cu, Ag, and Au. The nanoeffects are found to induce shifts of up to 0.3 eV in the linear scaling relationships between the binding energies of C-bound species on the catalyst surface. In contrast, the O-bound species exhibit a larger shift of up to 0.9 eV, particularly at metal-surface interfacial sites. The CO hydrogenation activity of unsupported metal nanoparticles and (211) surfaces is predicted to be enhanced compared with M(111) surfaces by as much as six orders of magnitude in the case of Au. For coinage metals, methanol synthesis is further enhanced by more than two orders of magnitude at the nanoparticle-support interface, while CO methanation on ZnO-supported Pt and Pd is accelerated by over four orders of magnitude relative to unsupported nanoparticles. In turn, Ir exhibits a significant enhancement of approximately two orders of magnitude in catalytic activity due to the reduction in coordination number, while the effect of ZnO amplifies its activity by an additional 50 times compared with M(211). As a result, the interfacial Cu/ZnO sites are calculated to have the highest activity for methanol synthesis, whereas the interfacial Ir/ZnO sites exhibit the highest CO methanation rate. This study serves as a proof-of-concept demonstration that nanoeffects, particularly nanoparticle-support interactions, can be leveraged to rationally design more active catalysts for emerging green energy technologies.

abstract: Rain-solar hybrid triboelectric-photovoltaic systems can simultaneously harvest energy from raindrop impacts on rainy days and sunlight on sunny days, enabling efficient energy conversion across diverse environmental conditions. However, integrating triboelectric rain cells (TRCs) with perovskite solar cells (PSC) often compromises light transmission through the glass substrate and reduces the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the solar cell. Given that the energy available from rainfall is low and intermittent, even minor PCE losses in the solar cells can offset any potential net gain. Here, we overcome this trade-off by integrating a TRC onto a PSC using a new top ITO-free device architecture in which an inverted pyramid-textured polydimethylsiloxane (P-PDMS) film on the glass substrate serves simultaneously as the triboelectric layer and the light-trapping structure. The P-PDMS layer also enables passive radiative cooling, helping preserve PCE during operation. This design increases the PCE for both solar cells and mini-modules, with the champion cell improving from 21.8 to 22.9% and the mini-module efficiency increasing from 18.5 to 19.7%. The P-PDMS triboelectric device also delivers a high open circuit voltage ( V oc-T ) of 80 V, a short-circuit current ( I sc-T ) of 114 μA, and an instantaneous power of 0.96 mW per droplet. Finally, we integrate the optimized triboelectric structure on a perovskite mini-module, demonstrating a practical route toward continuous, weather-independent energy harvesting under real-world conditions.

In situ electronic characterization of electrochemically tunable metal oxide nanostructures for energy applications via inverted scanning tunneling spectroscopy
abstract: An in situ methodology was developed and implemented to characterize electronic band properties at the apex of high-aspect-ratio nanoscale solid-state electrochemical devices. Model devices with materials relevant to various energy applications were composed of nano-thin metal oxide films coated onto metallic scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) probe tips. Electronic properties of these films at the device apex were measured by inverting the tunneling spectroscopy paradigm: vacuum tunneling spectroscopy between functionalized STM probe tips with ambiguous electronic properties and metallic substrates – a method we here introduce as inverted scanning tunneling spectroscopy (I-STS). Additionally, concentration of metal species within the apex of these metal-oxide devices can be controlled through nanoscale solid-state electrochemistry within the same experimental platform, allowing subsequent in situ I-STS measurements that directly reveal how electronic properties change with composition. We first demonstrated and validated the I-STS approach by quantifying the bandgap of nano-thin aluminum oxide ( ca . 7.1 eV). Next, bandgaps (or lack thereof) of nano-thin stoichiometric lithium cobalt oxide (LCO, ca . 1.6 eV) and deeply sub-stoichiometric LCO (0 eV) were observed, directly measuring LCO band evolution along its delithiation-induced semiconductor-to-metal transition. I-STS reveals bandgaps at the nanoscale apex that are substantially narrower than bulk values, demonstrating pronounced modulation of electronic structure in electrochemically active oxide nanostructure termini. Ultimately, I-STS uniquely enables electrical characterization of small, high-aspect-ratio model devices at their apex – a spatial regime inaccessible with existing techniques – and provides a pathway to explore ion-coupled electronic phenomena in advanced energy storage and low-power neuromorphic computing devices using standard STM instrumentation.

abstract: Reducing heat losses is essential for improving energy efficiency of thermally driven separation processes such as membrane distillation (MD). Membrane material enhancements offer huge potential in this regard. Conventional MD membranes typically suffer from relatively high thermal conductivity, which limits both water production rates and energy performance. In this work, we discuss the fabrication of polyvinylidene fluoride–reduced graphene oxide (PVDF–rGO) mixed matrix membrane using rGO microgranules that promote a hierarchical pore structure. The membrane’s combination of nanoscale and microscale pores, together with the phonon-scattering effects introduced by the dispersed rGO microgranules, result in an ultralow effective thermal conductivity of 0.04 W/mK which is among the lowest reported for MD membranes. The membrane, fabricated via phase inversion, exhibits high porosity (91%) and favorable morphology for vapor transport. Experimental testing in air gap MD (AGMD) achieved a permeate flux of 5.44 LMH at 80 °C, while comprehensive modeling of both AGMD and conductive gap MD (CGMD) configurations revealed that lowering thermal conductivity directly enhances not only flux but also energy efficiency, with CGMD showing particularly strong sensitivity. The gained output ratio (GOR) versus flux analysis further establishes low-conductivity membranes as a key design paradigm for advancing MD toward sustainable and scalable water treatment. By demonstrating a pathway to suppress conductive heat losses through low membrane thermal conductivity, this work establishes a new benchmark for membrane design in high-efficiency desalination technologies.

abstract: Harvesting energy from ultra-low-frequency and low-steepness ocean waves remains a great challenge for triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) because conventional contact–separation modes produce only transient pulses and cannot maintain output under slow excitations. Here, we present a bamboo-copter-inspired helical-rod-driven cylindrical TENG (HRC-TENG), in which an annular clutch with a face-ratchet engagement converts the axial reciprocating motion of the helical rod into continuous rotation. This design transforms the intermittent contact–separation behavior into a sliding mode, enabling the device to deliver high-intensity electrical output (~546 V) continuously for ~12 s upon a single external excitation. The HRC-TENG achieves a frequency-normalized volumetric power density of 2.84 W/m³/Hz at 0.1 Hz, surpassing that reported previously for cylindrical TENG-based wave energy harvesters. Coupling between wave excitation, structural motion, and electricity generation under realistic ocean conditions was enhanced by employing a hydrodynamic-based model, validated using an active-absorption wave tank, and further confirmed by successfully illuminating 532 high-brightness LEDs during a quiet period of ocean activity in Sanya Bay (China). The proposed design is expected to inspire future development of wave energy harvesting devices, and to offer broad prospects for scalable, self-powered marine sensing networks.

abstract: Porous biocarbons possess special features, such as well-developed and tunable porosity, and adjustable surface chemistry, which make them standout candidates for supercapacitors. Heteroatom doping, such as sulfur (S), nitrogen (N), and oxygen (O), further enhances energy storage capacity and stability. Herein, we present a versatile method for synthesizing in situ heteroatom-doped porous carbons by integrating solid-state activation and thiourea doping. Material optimization was achieved by varying the amount of thiourea used for doping during activation. This approach successfully incorporates multiple heteroatoms, including N, S, and O, into the carbon framework, yielding an optimized, high-surface-area (3494 m² g⁻¹) and large-pore-volume (1.86 cm³ g⁻¹) material, THBC-2. These features contribute to an exceptional 3E capacitance (373 F g⁻¹/0.5 A g⁻¹) in 3 M KOH. Additionally, THBC-2 was evaluated as a zinc-ion capacitor (ZIC) cathode, achieving impressive energy cum power densities (101 Wh kg⁻¹ and 399 W kg⁻¹) and good cycling stability. Ex situ characterization during charge/discharge processes provided valuable insights into the formation and dissolution of intermediate phases, which influence the stability and performance of the ZIC system. The materials presented demonstrate strong potential for use in supercapacitors and can be extended to other electrochemical applications.

abstract: Harvesting low-frequency, stochastic, and multidirectional environmental energy remains challenging due to the directional dependence, insufficient current output, and intermittent operation of single-mode generators. Here, we report a triboelectric-electromagnetic-solar hybrid generator (TESHG) featuring a three-layer tapered architecture that integrates contact-separation triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) arrays, electromagnetic generator (EMG) units, and a top-mounted solar cell within a fully enclosed, blade-free body. Unlike conventional bladed wind turbines, this design offers excellent bio-friendliness by eliminating risks to flying wildlife. Fluid-structure simulations reveal that an inverted-trapezoidal shell intensifies vortex-induced vibration for efficient self-excited oscillation. To overcome the intermittency and temporal fluctuations inherent in high-entropy energy sources, the TESHG enables complementary utilization of wind, wave, and solar energy. One TENG unit delivers 5.24 mW peak power; the EMG reaches 0.65 mW under matched load. The device maintains stable output under variable wind/wave conditions, preserves performance after 5,000,000 cycles, and tolerates temperature/humidity variations. The TESHG enables faster charging than any single mode alone, with demonstrations in self-powered lighting, environmental monitoring, smart agriculture, and hydrogen generation. This work provides a compact, bio-friendly, all-weather strategy for harvesting wind, wave, and solar energy in both marine and land-based environments, offering a promising solution for distributed self-powered systems such as rural households, farms, island stations, remote base stations, and urban rooftops, where conventional wind turbines are infeasible.

abstract: In this work Zn-HHTP nanoflower structured metal organic framework (MOF) is prepared by controlling the deprotonation during solvothermal reaction for the development of next-generation energy storage devices. Here, the Zn-HHTP synthesised at a 10:84 NaOH-to-Zn weight ratio (ZH3) exhibited a flower-like morphology with excellent crystallinity and wettability (35° contact angle), thereby enhancing the electrochemical performance of flexible energy storage. The three-electrode measurement analysis shows that the prepared ZH3 materials exhibit a specific capacitance of 18 F.g ⁻1 and an energy density of 2.5 W.h.kg ⁻1 at 1 mV.s ⁻1 . Using ZH3 as the active material, a symmetrical flexible electrochemical capacitor (EC) is developed, and its performance is compared separately with salt-in-water (SIW) and water-in-salt (WIS) electrolytes. The ZH3-WIS device outperformed the ZH3-SIW system by suppressing water decomposition and extending the operating voltage beyond the 1.23 V limit of conventional SIW electrolytes, thereby significantly enhancing energy density. The ZH3-WIS EC achieved an operating voltage of 2.0 V, a capacitance of 5.9 F.g ⁻1 , and an energy density of 3.28 W.h.kg ⁻1 , with 72.69% capacity retention after 6,000 cycles. The device also demonstrated excellent mechanical flexibility under different bending angles. Practical applicability was validated through successful integration into low-power electronic systems. These results highlight the potential of fabricated ECs to advance safe, high-voltage aqueous systems, establishing a flexible energy storage platform suitable for wearable electronics.

abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable flexible sensors serve as a fundamental platform for the accurate acquisition and real-time monitoring of physiological signals. Fiber-based triboelectric nanogenerators (F-TENGs) are promising candidates for physiological monitoring applications due to their intrinsic advantages, including mechanical flexibility, high integrability, and inherent self-powered capability. However, advanced fiber-based TENGs commonly suffer from insufficient interfacial adhesion between the dielectric layer and the electrode core, which triggers spontaneous interfacial delamination. This failure mechanism directly causes significant degradation in sensing accuracy, stability, and long-term durability. Herein, we report a fiber-based silk fibroin triboelectric nanogenerator (FSF-TENG) featuring superior interfacial robustness, exceptional stability, and enhanced output, fabricated by leveraging strong intermolecular interactions between a biocompatible silk fibroin dielectric layer and a flexible PEDOT:PSS@PVA hydrogel electrode. When integrated as a sensing unit within flexible textile substrates, the FSF-TENG exhibits a multistage linear sensitivity profile with a pressure sensitivity of 0.3838 kPa -1 , enabling real-time and precise monitoring of critical human respiratory physiological signals. This work establishes a scalable, continuous fabrication route for F-TENGs, providing innovative and practical strategies for the rational design and large-scale production of high-stability, self-powered flexible sensor systems.

title: Nanoarchitectonics of borophene via fluorination-mediated transition-metal doping for oxygen evolution electrocatalysis
abstract: Borophene is a polymorphic metallic Xene with record electronic mobility in its β 12 phase, which exhibits record electronic mobility and Young’s modulus along its ridgelines, which are indeed better than graphene which renders it a unique quantum material, extremely useful for numerous frontline applications including ultrafast electronic chips, wearable electronic gadgets, THz electronics and ultrafast sensors. With atomic vacancies in its lattice, a unique feature in borophene among all Xenes, enables its edge atoms to be catalytically active, and therefore, it is deemed as the next generation electrocatalyst. Transition metal doping can help inject electrons into the borophene lattice which inherently lacks electrons, thereby enabling it for catalytic performance. However, it is extremely challenging to substitutionally dope borophene due to strong lattice binding. Here, we demonstrate a fluorination-mediated controlled approach employing exotic thermodynamic conditions which enables facile, tunable doping of borophene, producing Fe-doped (Fe-FB1, Fe-FB2, Fe-FB3), Ni-doped (Ni-FB1, Ni-FB2, Ni-FB3), and FeNi-codoped fluoroborophene (FeNi-FB) electrocatalysts. Notably, the FeNi-FB co-doped catalyst exhibits a synergistic enhancement in oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity, delivering a low overpotential of 0.274 V at 10 mA cm⁻², compared with 0.306 V and 0.310 V for Fe-FB and Ni-FB, respectively. Post-OER characterizations established robust FeNi-FB electrodes under alkaline condition catalytic performance. These findings establish fluorination-mediated doping as an efficient strategy for engineering high-performance borophene-based electrocatalysts.

abstract: Cost of Pt still limits the scale-up of proton-exchange-membrane (PEM) water electrolysis. The challenge is not merely to use less Pt, but to sustain high HER activity and durability at ultralow Pt supply. Here we develop a cathode based on a noble-metal-free, acid-tolerant Zr-based metallic glass with an ultralow-Pt layer. Elliptical vibration chiseling patterns the bulk substrate in one step into a three-level architecture of millimeter grooves, micrometer ribs and sub-100-nm shear bands, followed by Pt deposition via magnetron sputtering. The architecture boosts Pt utilization through complementary roles: micro ribs increase accessible surface area; shear bands guide Pt nucleation into defect-rich nanocrystals with abundant boundary sites; and millimeter grooves promote bubble removal and electrolyte renewal, mitigating bubble-induced instabilities. Meanwhile, sputtered Pt forms a direct metallic bond with the metallic glass, improving interfacial conduction and adhesion under load. With only 20.06 μg cm−2 Pt, the cathode delivers 46 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in acid and shows 1.7% decay over 100 h at 100 mA cm−2, together with a 97.79% reduction in peak-to-peak current fluctuations versus the polished surface. These results outline a scalable route to ultralow-Pt PEM cathodes by co-engineering structure, site exposure and mass transport.

abstract: With the rapid expansion of the Internet of Things, there is growing demand for low-cost and sustainable self-powered human–computer interaction systems. This study proposes a single-electrode triboelectric interface fabricated by toner printing using a conventional laser printer. Toner patterns are printed on a transparent PVC sheet and generate electrical signals through finger sliding based on triboelectric effects of the human body. The toner acts as an insulating mask that geometrically limits contact between skin and PVC, enabling deterministic control of charge generation in both space and time. This strategy significantly improves signal-to-noise ratio and waveform reproducibility compared with conventional free-contact approaches. The output voltage can be precisely programmed by adjusting geometric parameters such as pattern width, spacing, and number. Surface inspection confirmed no visible wear of the toner film, and stable signals were maintained after 1000 sliding cycles without degradation. By quantitatively linking waveform peak widths and intervals to geometric parameters, slide-speed estimation was achieved with an error of 3.5% or less relative to measured values. A real-time recognition system enabled direction detection and binary input using peak detection, and machine learning classification reached over 89% accuracy for printed-pattern recognition, alphabet input, and user identification. Because the method relies only on a standard printing process and requires no complex wiring, it provides a simple, low-cost, and energy-efficient platform suitable for wearable electronics and secure interaction devices. The proposed framework offers a scalable approach for customizable tactile interfaces in future distributed sensing environments.

abstract: Solar-driven CO 2 reduction offers a sustainable pathway to alleviate carbon emissions while producing value-added fuels; however, its efficiency is often limited by sluggish surface reaction kinetics. Here, we report local coordination environment tuning as an effective strategy for modulating reaction energetics in halide perovskites. We identify that CO 2 -to-CO conversion on Cs 3 Bi 2 Br 9 is hindered by electronically localized active sites and limited surface redox reactivity, which restrict charge delocalization, weaken ⁎CO 2 adsorption, and impede the formation of ⁎COOH − the key rate-determining intermediate. To overcome this bottleneck, Sb heteroatoms are introduced to regulate the reaction microenvironment and modulate local electronic interactions at catalytic sites. Theoretical calculations and experimental analyses reveal that microenvironment regulation promotes orbital rehybridization, enhances CO 2 adsorption and facilitates ⁎COOH formation, thereby accelerating proton-coupled electron transfer. As a result, the optimized catalyst enables efficient and selective CO 2 photoreduction without sacrificial agents, achieving a CO generation rate of 106.2 μmol g −1 h −1 with near-unity selectivity.

title: Effective removal of ICP etching damage at the GaN regrowth interface through MOCVD in-situ cleaning
abstract: This work demonstrates that in-situ tertiarybutylchloride (TBCl) cleaning in Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) can effectively remove the inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching damage at the gallium nitride (GaN) regrowth interface. Two distinct TBCl in-situ cleaning modes can be observed that a smooth surface enables step-flow-mode cleaning for effective removal of ICP etching damage, while a rough surface results in 3D-mode cleaning with incomplete elimination. Quasi-vertical PN diodes with regrown p-GaN on ICP-etched n-GaN were fabricated. The PN diodes with the regrowth interface treated by TBCl shown a suppressed leakage current, reduced ideality factor, and improved breakdown voltage. Temperature-dependent leakage current analysis reveals that the ICP-etched samples show both variable-range hopping (VRH) and Poole–Frenkel emission (PFE), while TBCl-treated samples only exhibit PFE, confirming that the altered leakage behavior stems from the effective removal of the ICP etching damage. This work provides a reliable strategy for vertical GaN power devices which requires regrowth process.

title: Structurally chiral meta-tribomaterials for mechanical sequence programming via electrical decoding and interactive control
abstract: Chained compression-twist metamaterials are programmable mechanical architectures whose information is typically read out by visual inspection, which leads to kinematic degeneracy and challenges in black box recognition. Here, we propose an integrated metamaterial-triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) system, embedding a dual-rotor disk TENG within a bilayer metamaterial with variable stiffness, enabling reliable electrical readout of structural sequences. Under impact loading, the system identifies frequencies ranging from 1 to 6 Hz, and distinguishes displacement amplitudes between 5 and 25 mm at 4 Hz. An array-based mechanical password lock is further developed, which, under random pressing, employs Region of Interest (ROI)-based extraction to isolate effective intervals and applies Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)-based adaptive matching for template enrollment and single-channel unlocking. Based on this capability, the “11”, “00”, “10”, and “01” configurations are mapped to forward, reverse, left, and right commands, respectively, thereby translating structural codes into vehicle motions for interactive control. This work establishes a scalable framework for embodied intelligent mechanical systems that integrate buffering, vibration mitigation, electrical sensing, and machine to machine coordination.

abstract: Flexible self-powered systems are often limited by material incompatibilities among sensing, energy harvesting, and storage units. Here, we present a Cl--selective hybrid hydrogel that integrates these functions within a single soft material. The hydrogel consists of a sodium alginate/polyacrylamide dual network reinforced with hydroxyl-functionalized multi-walled carbon nanotubes in a glycerol/EMIMCl solvent. Density functional theory indicates that hydroxyl-functionalized nanotubes preferentially interact with Cl- over EMIM+, creating a selective interfacial environment that facilitates coupled ionic and electronic transport. Leveraging this mechanism, the hydrogel simultaneously functions as a strain, pressure, and temperature sensor, a triboelectric nanogenerator electrode, and a compatible electrolyte for flexible supercapacitors. The strain sensor exhibits a gauge factor up to 5.67, the triboelectric device delivers an open-circuit voltage of 171 V and a peak power density of 49 µW·cm-2, and the hydrogel-based supercapacitors maintain over 96% Coulombic efficiency across 10,000 cycles. Using a single material across energy harvesting and storage units minimizes interfacial mismatch, enabling closed-loop operation from −40 to 40°C. Additionally, the output signals support machine-learning-assisted impact recognition, demonstrating a proof-of-concept intelligent interface. This work establishes a material-centric strategy for self-powered electronics by integrating transport, mechanics, and multifunctionality within a unified soft matter system.

abstract: ABSTRACT High-entropy perovskite oxides offer a versatile platform for electrocatalysis, yet the lack of quantitative structural descriptors has limited predictive design in these compositionally complex systems. Here, we establish orthorhombicity as a simple and transferable structural descriptor that enables rational control of lattice distortion in high-entropy perovskite oxides. By systematically tuning the A-site ionic radius in a series of A(CrMnFeCoNi)O 3 perovskites, including a ten-cation high-entropy composition, we achieve predictable modulation of crystal symmetry and octahedral tilting while maintaining single-phase structures. We identify an intermediate distortion regime that delivers optimal oxygen evolution reaction activity with (LaNdSmGdY)(CrMnFeCoNi)O 3 , which displays 2.1 times higher activity at a potential of 1.6 V and 3.4 times greater stability at a current density of 10 mA cm -2 than the average activity and stability of the five A(CrMnFeCoNi)O 3 catalysts. More broadly, this work demonstrates orthorhombicity as an important design descriptor for engineering high-entropy perovskite electrocatalysts with controllable properties based on the control over single- and multiple-phased solid-state structures.

abstract: The integration of efficient energy harvesting and precise biomechanical sensing is essential for the development of sustainable wearable electronics. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are attractive candidates because they intrinsically combine mechanical energy conversion and force sensing capabilities. However, achieving high output together with robust stability under harsh physiological conditions, especially across extreme temperature, remains challenging. Herein, we report an environmentally adaptable three-dimensional (3D) composite aerogel, denoted as FG/CS/Ti3C2Tx (FCT), fabricated from Ti3C2Tx MXene, chitosan (CS), and fish gelatin (FG) via freeze-drying. The CS/FG framework provides a dynamic hydrogen-bond network rich in tribo-positive functional groups. Meanwhile, the inclusion of Ti3C2Tx enhances dielectric modulation and interfacial polarization to synergistically boost the triboelectric performance. Benefiting from a stable architecture and reversible hydrogen bonding, the aerogel achieves self-healing within 30 s with a trace amount of deionized water to fully restore the electrical output. Moreover, the porous and solvent-free framework offers thermal insulation that mitigates temperature-dependent charge-transport variations, which enables stable operation from -80 ℃ to 60 ℃. In addition, a derived Arrhenius-type charge-decay equation establishes a quantitative relationship between temperature, storage time, and surface charge retention, corresponding to over 90% retention after 48 h of isothermal holding. After coupling with functionalized fluorinated PDMS (FPDMS), the device delivers a peak power density of 714.69 mW m-2, which surpasses recently reported aerogel-based TENGs. This platform enables self-powered monitoring of fingertip tapping, joint motions, gait, and respiration. Furthermore, a pulse-monitoring alert system is developed to capture subtle arterial pulsation signals. The system identifies fine-grained pulse-wave features, including percussion, tidal, and diastolic waves. With a physiological-threshold algorithm, the system achieves real-time heart-rate monitoring and triggers alarms upon detecting abnormalities. This work establishes a comprehensive route from functional material design to integrated system implementation, and offers a practical strategy for self-driven health monitoring.

title: Triboelectric–mechanical decoupling in porous polymer composites for self-powered biomechanical sensing
abstract: Porous polymer composites are emerging as promising triboelectric materials for self-powered biomechanical sensing because they integrate mechanical softness with effective electrical output. Their porous architectures endow them with low and tunable Young’s modulus for compliant interfacing with biological surfaces, while deformation-induced contact and separation of internal pore surfaces give rise to triboelectric charge generation. However, compositional engineering that enhances triboelectric output often simultaneously increases stiffness, creating a fundamental tradeoff between electrical performance and mechanical compliance. Despite growing efforts to address this challenge, a unifying framework for understanding and resolving this tradeoff remains lacking. In this review, a tribo-dipole framework is introduced to correlate porous architecture and material composition with triboelectric output through dipole density, charge magnitude, separation distance, and spatial ordering. Building on this framework, a systematic decoupling perspective is established to rationalize the output–modulus tradeoff and to organize practical strategies for selectively enhancing electrical performance while preserving low Young’s modulus. Finally, current challenges and future directions are discussed for advanced self-powered applications, including wearable sensors and implantable therapeutic devices.

abstract: Tin-lead (Sn-Pb) mixed halide perovskites are imperative to fabricate high-performance all-perovskite tandem solar cells. However, the rapid, light-induced oxidation of Sn 2+ severely limits their operational longevity. Here, we uncover an effective antioxidant strategy using zero-valent tin nanoparticles to intercept these degradation pathways. The zero-valent tin nanoparticles exhibit a potent reductive capacity that eliminates deleterious Sn 4+ impurities during precursor processing and thin film crystallization via a redox-shutting mechanism. Operando photoluminescence and stability analyses substantiate that zero-valent tin nanoparticles form robust Sn–I bonds with photo-generated I 2 species, thereby decoupling the I 2 -mediated Sn 2+ oxidation cycle. Furthermore, the zero-valent tin modification facilitates photo-induced stress relaxation, leading to a transient initial efficiency enhancement. Subsequently, zero-valent tin-modified FA 0.7 MA 0.3 Sn 0.5 Pb 0.5 I 3 based inverted planar solar cells achieve a certified power conversion efficiency of 23.26% (aperture area 4.05 mm 2 ), maintaining over 90% of their initial performance after 500 hours of continuous operation at the maximum power point under AM 1.5 G illumination. Notably, the unencapsulated Sn-Pb perovskite devices exhibited environmental durability, retaining over 80% of their initial efficiency after six days of ambient exposure at 60% relative humidity. This work provides a simple yet scalable chemical approach to overcome the oxidation bottleneck, paving the way for commercially viable, stable Sn-containing perovskite optoelectronics.

abstract: ABSTRACT Solar-driven photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to highly reduced, energy-dense oxygenated products is hindered by sluggish proton-coupled electron transfer and hydrogenation steps. Conventional strategies that separate redox centers reduce charge recombination but limit proton transfer from water oxidation. Here, we address this trade-off by constructing dopant-defect-coupled Frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) in CdS quantum dots (QDs) by controlled Cu doping. Cu⁺ dopant and adjacent surface vacancies form Cu⁺–Vₛ pairs that generate strong interfacial electric dipoles, enabling polarized activation of O–H bonds in water and C–O bonds in adsorbed CO*. Time-resolved spectroscopic studies demonstrate these FLPs can spatially stabilize photogenerated holes and electrons at the ground state Lewis basic site and the neighboring Lewis acid site, respectively, without rapid charge recombination. In-situ FTIR and theoretical calculations confirm that such FLPs enhance water oxidation through O–H bond polarized cleavage, creating a proton-rich environment while simultaneously promoting CO* hydrogenation at nearby reduction sites to form key intermediates (HCO* and H 3 CO*), leading to improved production of highly reduced oxygenated products. Consequently, the optimally doped QDs demonstrate robust stability over five consecutive cycles, alongside a 1.4-fold enhancement in the total yield of oxygenated products over pure CdS and 94% overall selectivity for highly reduced oxygenated products.

abstract: Dentin regeneration remains a key clinical challenge due to the lack of bioactive materials capable of dynamically regulating the native microenvironment. A multifunctional piezoelectric scaffold that integrates mechanical reinforcement, piezoelectric stimulation, bioactive ion release, biomineralization, and antibacterial activity is developed by embedding strontium-polyoxometalate (Sr-POM) subnanowires (SNWs) into a poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) matrix. Sr-POM SNWs incorporation enhances PVDF’s piezoelectric β-phase content by 67.54%, boosting piezoelectric output voltage by ~2900%, and reinforcing the piezoelectric scaffold (68.83% tensile strength and 198% toughness increases). The scaffold generates local electrical potentials under mechanical stimulation to activate cellular ion channels, sustainably releases Sr2+ to promote odontogenic differentiation of human dental pulp stem cells, and PW12O403- to guide hydroxyapatite mineralization, with enhanced piezoelectricity disrupting bacterial membranes. In vitro, the piezoelectric scaffold promotes cell adhesion, differentiation, and mineralization, while in vivo it exhibits good biosafety, upregulates dentin sialophosphoprotein expression and induces dentin regeneration in a rat pulp-capping model. This integrated strategy couples biophysical and biochemical cues, offering a promising platform for functional dentin repair.

abstract: The plateau capacity of hard carbon (HC) dictates the energy density of sodium ion batteries, but is severely limited by open pore defects generated during the pyrolysis of precursors. Herein, we propose an in-situ pore sealing strategy to successfully construct a closed pore enriched HC via the synergistic co-pyrolysis of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and coal tar (CT). During the pyrolysis process, the low softening point CT uniformly coats the surface of the CMC skeleton and constructs a dense cross-linked network with the radicals generated from CMC pyrolysis, effectively retarding the rapid escape of volatiles. Concurrently, leveraging the thermal shrinkage effect of CT at elevated temperatures, the nascent open pores are seamlessly sealed in situ. This interfacial synergy endows the material with an exceptional closed pore volume of 0.1280 cm3 g-1 and an average pore diameter of 2.99 nm. Furthermore, the induced long range pseudo graphitic nanoribbons provide ultrafast Na+ diffusion channels, facilitating the dense accumulation of quasi metallic sodium clusters within these closed pores. Consequently, the CMC-CT anode has 343.98 mAh g-1 high capacity and retains 84.26% capacity after 1000 cycles at 1500 mA g-1. Validated by a stable Na3V2(PO4)3‖CMC-CT full cell, this scalable pore engineering paradigm holds great promise for next generation energy storage.

title: Reversible thermally-switchable chirality of circularly polarized luminescence in perovskite nanocrystals enabled by cholesteric liquid crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Circularly polarized (CP) luminescence provides an additional degree of freedom for emerging integrated photonic and communication technologies, yet reversible switching of its handedness remains challenging as it is fundamentally constrained by the need to reconfigure chiral emitters. Here, we break this limitation by introducing a thermally programmable photonic strategy that enables reversible switching of CP light (right or left) without modifying the emitters themselves. This is achieved through modular heterostructure integration of perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs) with bilayer cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs) of opposite handedness, where the CLCs function as dynamic chiral photonic filters. The switching mechanism is governed by temperature-driven spectral translation of the CLC photonic bandgaps (PBGs), arising from the thermally induced variation of the helical pitch that shifts the Bragg reflection wavelength. As the PBGs sequentially resonate with the narrowband emission of PNCs, selective suppression of opposite circular polarizations occurs, leading to deterministic inversion of CP luminescence handedness. The system delivers a large g lum of up to 1.84 and reversible dissymmetry switching ( Δ g lum > 3.3, Δ g lum = ∣ g lum + ∣ + ∣ g lum − ∣ ) across the visible spectrum. This work establishes a general photonic strategy for thermally programmable CP light handedness and holds promise for applications in adaptive photonic systems, secure optical communication, and advanced information technologies.

abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are useful for large-scale energy storage because they are safe, low-cost, and environmentally friendly. However, Zn anodes still face many problems, such as dendrite growth, corrosion, hydrogen evolution, and byproduct buildup. These problems reduce battery cycling stability. Inspired by the “soft-interior and rigid-exterior” structure of natural nacre, we constructed a ZIF-71@PMN dual-layer composite interface on a Zn surface using a polymer-induced interfacial nucleation method. The inner PMN layer is rich in carbonyl and lactam groups. It strongly coordinates with Zn2+, promotes desolvation, improves interfacial adhesion, and provides nucleation sites for ZIF-71. It also works as a flexible buffer. The outer ZIF-71 layer has clear micropores, a rigid framework, and hydrophobic properties. This makes the Zn2+ flux more uniform, blocks water molecules, and reduces side reactions. Theoretical analyzes together with finite element simulations reveal that the constructed interface effectively promotes Zn2+ desolvation while simultaneously regulating the electric field and ion concentration distribution towards greater uniformity. As a result, the ZIF-71@PMN@Zn symmetric cell achieves long-term stable operation exceeding 5000 h at 1 mA cm-2 and over 1500 h at 4 mA cm-2. Moreover, at 5 A g-1, the full cell coupled with AlVO-NMP delivers 91.9% capacity retention after 4000 cycles, whereas the soft-pack battery retains 81.4% capacity after 3000 cycles, highlighting its remarkable potential for practical applications.

abstract: With the accelerating demand for critical minerals and the imminent surge of end-of-life lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), efficient recycling technologies are urgently needed to secure a sustainable resource supply and enable a circular battery economy. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) offer an environmentally benign pathway for metal recovery, yet their practical implementation is constrained by inherently slow leaching rates. In this study, microwave-responsive DESs were rationally designed using choline chloride as a common, low-cost hydrogen-bond acceptor, while varying the hydrogen-bond donor to tune acidity, metal coordination, and leaching performance. Among the DESs investigated, choline chloride-lactic acid delivered the highest metal recovery, achieving >99% extraction of Co and Mn and >92% extraction of Li and Ni from industrial LIB black mass within only 30 min at 200 °C under microwave irradiation. The exceptional performance is attributed to rapid volumetric heating and enhanced solvent-solid interactions, which accelerate mass transfer and metal dissolution. Combined spectroscopic and thermal analyses revealed a ligand-assisted leaching mechanism involving proton-mediated metal-oxygen bond cleavage and stabilization of dissolved metal species through chloride-lactate coordination. The DES maintained high leaching efficiency over multiple recycling cycles and enabled downstream metal separation via selective precipitation. Life cycle assessment confirmed the environmental viability of the process and identified energy consumption as the primary hotspot for future optimization. This study establishes a rapid, energy-efficient, and environmentally benign microwave-assisted solvo-metallurgical strategy for the sustainable recovery of critical metals from spent LIBs.

abstract: Resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based on metal-halide perovskites has attracted significant interest for neuromorphic and in-memory computing applications owing to its simple structure and tunable material properties. However, practical implementation is limited by stochastic filament formation and the lack of effective control parameters beyond electrical bias and light intensity. Here, we introduce light polarization as an independent control variable for resistive switching using a chiral perovskite RRAM device. Owing to the intrinsic circular dichroism of the chiral perovskite, right- and left-circularly polarized light (RCP and LCP) generate different photocarrier populations under identical illumination intensity, enabling deterministic modulation of switching behavior. As a result, the set voltage (Vset) is reduced from 0.15 V in the dark to 0.10 V and 0.05 V under RCP and LCP, respectively, accompanied by improved switching uniformity. Conduction mechanism analysis reveals that polarization-dependent photocarrier generation induces a transition from interface-limited to bulk-dominated transport, thereby stabilizing filament nucleation. In addition, the incorporation of bulky chiral ligands, which enhances chirality, leads to enlarged interlayer spacing that facilitates uniform Ag ion infiltration and suppresses stochastic filament formation. Finally, polarization-modulated synaptic characteristics are demonstrated, and artificial neural network simulations show enhanced learning performance. These results demonstrate that polarization-driven control of resistive switching can be effectively reinforced by structural engineering, establish light polarization as a new control knob for resistive switching, and provide a viable pathway toward multifunctional memory and neuromorphic applications.

abstract: The prolonged operation of high-energy-density lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs) hinges on reactivating irreversible Li (i.e., dead Li comprises isolated-Li0 debris and residual SEI), not just preventing its formation. However, concurrently achieving dead-Li suppression and rejuvenation remains challenging. Here, we design an N-doped hierarchically porous carbon (NHPC) host that enables bottom-up, uniform Li deposition via its interconnected ordered porosity and lithiophilic N-dopant sites, reducing dead Li formation. Notably, the lifespans of LiFePO4 cells using NHPC hosted Li is increased by 3 times, where limited dead Li that is dominated by isolated Li0 (a more reactivatable dead Li source) accumulates in NHPC. The porous structure of NHPC induces thin solid-electrolyte interphase, spatially confines dead Li and provides abundant electronic conducting pathways. These features collectively promote the electronic reconnection of isolated Li0 with the electrode by applying a facile resting protocol, recovering 28.3% Li loss and further extending the lifespan of NHPC@Cu||LiFePO4 cells by another ~100%. The feasibility of NHPC host can further be translated into low-temperature and pouch cells that suffer worse dead-Li issues. This work offers a new design perspective for functional hosts to revive dead Li and advance long-life Li metal batteries.

abstract: Quasi solid-state lithium metal batteries are promising next-generation energy storage systems owing to their high energy density and enhanced safety. However, severe interfacial incompatibility between solid electrolytes and electrodes, along with uneven lithium deposition, remains a major obstacle to their practical application. Herein, a heterostructured bilayer composite solid electrolyte, in which metal-organic frameworks and Li₆.₂₈La₃Al₀.₂₄Zr₂O₁₂ (LLAZO) were incorporated into two respective layers, was constructed via electrospinning combined with in-situ photopolymerization on a polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber scaffold. LLAZO was incorporated into the cathode-facing layer to enhance oxidative stability, while UiO-66 was introduced into the anode-facing layer to regulate Li⁺ transport and suppress anion migration. The PAN nanofiber scaffold provided robust mechanical support and enables precise thickness control, while continuous in-situ polymerization ensured intimate interfacial contact between the electrolyte layers and the electrodes, thereby minimizing interfacial resistance and facilitating efficient lithium-ion transport. As a result, the heterostructured bilayer electrolyte delivered a high ionic conductivity of 5.18 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ and a Li⁺ transference number of 0.62 at room temperature. The Li||Li symmetric cell maintained stable lithium plating/stripping for over 2000 h. Moreover, Li||LiFePO₄ and Li||NCM811 full cells retained 90.0% and 82.7% of their initial capacities after 450 and 200 cycles at 1 C, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of this heterostructured bilayer electrolyte design for high-performance quasi solid-state lithium metal batteries.

Edge-synergistic Ni single atoms on MoS2 nanoflake islands enable tandem polysulfide electrocatalysis in lithium–sulfur batteries
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer a compelling pathway to accelerate sulfur redox reactions in lithium–sulfur batteries; however, their catalytic efficiency is often constrained by insufficient electronic regulation and unstable coordination environments under operating conditions. Herein, we report a nanoisland-confined single-atom strategy, where isolated Ni atoms are atomically anchored on MoS2 nanoflake islands and integrated within a reduced graphene oxide (rGO) matrix, forming a hierarchical Ni–MoS2@rGO electrocatalyst. In this architecture, Ni single atoms serve as highly active catalytic centers, while MoS2 nanoislands provide abundant exposed edge sites for LiPS adsorption and conversion, and rGO ensures fast electron transport and structural integrity. The strong Ni–MoS2 interactions optimize electronic structure, enabling rapid Li2S nucleation and decomposition, as confirmed by DFT calculations. In situ Raman and XRD studies reveal accelerated and reversible S8/Li2S phase transformations, demonstrating efficient suppression of the polysulfide shuttle. When employed as a functional cathode interlayer, Ni–MoS2@rGO delivers an excellent long-term cycling stability over 500 cycles with only 0.08% capacity decay per cycle, and robust rate performance. This work highlights the synergistic interplay between single atoms, nanoisland substrates, and conductive microsea networks, providing a generalizable platform for designing high-efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced lithium–sulfur batteries.

Polarity and symmetry engineering enables lateral MoS2 p-n homojunctions for polarization-sensitive self-powered photodetection and array imaging
abstract: Precise and nondestructive carrier-polarity reconfiguration and symmetry modulation in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors are essential for high-performance, polarization-sensitive homojunction optoelectronics. However, strategies capable of achieving both of the objectives simultaneously remain scarce, hindering the development of multifunctional homojunction optoelectronics. Here, a synergistic interfacial-engineering strategy that integrates polarity and symmetry engineering via strong van der Waals (vdW) interfacial coupling with CrOCl is reported. By leveraging CrOCl-induced polarity engineering, local carrier polarity reconfiguration has been achieved within a single MoS2 flake, enabling the formation of a high-quality lateral p-n homojunction. The resulting built-in electric field suppresses dark current and enables efficient separation of photogenerated carriers under self-powered operation, yielding a responsivity of 0.74 A W−1. Interestingly, symmetry engineering at the MoS2/CrOCl interface induces local symmetry breaking in the contacted MoS2 region, giving rise to a polarization-sensitive photoresponse with a photocurrent anisotropy ratio of 1.81. Furthermore, a 3 × 3 pixel photodetector prototype integrated with a signal-conditioning circuit has been demonstrated, exhibiting low interpixel crosstalk and high-fidelity reconstruction of spatial optical fields carrying polarization information. This work provides a general framework for nondestructive polarity and symmetry engineering in 2D semiconductors toward multifunctional optoelectronics.

title: Constructing directional water nano-pathways in proton exchange membrane realizes holistic and flexible water management of fuel cells and water electrolyzers
abstract: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells and water electrolyzers require systematic water management for robust operation. However, current water management strategies only focus on single-side electrode and usual condition, lacking device-level overall and multi-status adaptive considerations. Herein, a nanocomposite PEM-presided strategy realizes holistic and flexible water management. Lamellar hydrophilic talcum is modified to produce magnetic-responsive nano-fillers, which are composited with Nafion matrix under magnetic field to construct PEMs with well-spread straight-forward water diffusion pathways along the membrane through-plane (TP) direction. This strategy accommodates rapid non-tortuous TP water diffusion in PEM, realizing overall water balance within holistic membrane electrode assembly under various conditions. Applied in devices, the TP-oriented nanocomposite PEM enables self-regulated well-deployed water management, which markedly promotes the electrochemical processes related to water/gas distribution and transfer, achieving 2026 mW cm-2 or 2.75 A cm-2 at 2 V for PEM fuel cell or water electrolyzer with little performance decay after 500 h harsh and variable operation. This nanocomposite PEM-presided holistic and flexible strategy offers shifting insight and efficacy for water management of fuel cells and water electrolyzers.

title: Contact-electro-dynamic therapy combats oral squamous cell carcinoma by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction and global metabolic collapse
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy, yet conventional reactive oxygen species (ROS)-based therapies are severely limited by their dependence on exogenous sensitizers and the hypoxic tumor microenvironment, necessitating a sensitizer-free and spatiotemporally controllable ROS generation strategy. F-SiO 2 microparticles with high biocompatibility were prepared, and ultrasonication was employed to initiate the contact-electro-catalysis (CEC) process between F-SiO 2 and surrounding body fluids for producing large amounts of ROS in the tumor lesion, which constitutes the core of our proposed contact-electro-dynamic therapy (CEDT) strategy. Mechanistic studies using whole transcriptome sequencing indicated that the ROS accumulation induced by CEDT led to a significant increase in oxidative stress levels within OSCC cells, subsequently causing severe mitochondrial dysfunction. This mitochondrial damage further led to severe disruption of cellular energy metabolism, manifested as a global metabolic collapse characterized by dual inhibition of glycolysis and lipid metabolism. Under this continuous metabolic collapse, the proliferation of OSCC cells was significantly inhibited, leading to massive apoptosis. In vitro and in vivo models confirmed that the CEDT enabled by F-SiO 2 microparticles demonstrated excellent biological safety and efficient tumor growth inhibition capabilities. This study not only provides a highly controllable and promising CEDT treatment paradigm for clinical intervention of OSCC, but also opens up new paths for biomedical applications based on interface electron transfer.

abstract: The development of multi-field synergistic catalysis has emerged as a critical frontier for maximizing energy utilization. However, performance of multi-field systems is often bottlenecked by inefficient charge-carrier migration arising from complex field coupling. Herein, we report a high-performance n-type TiO 2 /Ag 2.3 Se photothermoelectric (PTE) catalyst designed to overcome these transport limitations. By integrating thermoelectric functionality into the photocatalytic framework, we establish a 40°C temperature-gradient that triggers a robust Seebeck-driven internal electric field. This PTE coupling yields a photovoltage of 2.3 mV, significantly exceeding the linear summation of individual thermal (1.4 mV) and photo (0.3 mV) contributions. In-situ Raman spectroscopy and finite element method simulations reveal that the synergistic photothermal interaction induces a highly directional flux of charge carriers, effectively suppressing recombination and accelerating interfacial kinetics. Remarkably, the TiO 2 /Ag 2.3 Se composite achieves a photocatalytic degradation efficiency of 93%, far surpassing the combined totals of discrete photocatalysis (41%) and thermoelectric catalysis (13%). This pronounced “1 + 1 > 2” synergy demonstrates a paradigm shift in catalyst design, where wasted thermal energy is converted into a functional driving force for charge separation. This work not only provides deep mechanistic insights into thermal-induced interfacial charge transfer but also establishes a strategic framework for engineering waste-heat-driven micro-engines for self-powered environmental sustainability.

abstract: Secure and low-power identity authentication remains a key challenge for intelligent security systems. Here, we report a self-powered dual-modal intelligent password lock enabled by triboelectric nanogenerators (TENG). A TENG sensor array simultaneously encodes password sequences and dynamic bio-behavioral features, including signal amplitude, dwell time, and inter-keystroke intervals. Machine learning is employed to model these multi-channel signals for user-specific behavioral recognition. To enhance security while preserving privacy, a camera is activated only upon password confirmation to perform gesture-based verification. By integrating password correctness, behavioral patterns, and gesture recognition, a three-tier authentication framework is achieved. This system delivers low power consumption, strong resistance to spoofing, and minimal data leakage, providing a promising strategy for next-generation self-powered, multimodal intelligent security systems.

title: Sustainable cellulose nanofibrils as ultrasound-driven piezoelectric interfaces for wireless neuromodulation
abstract: Wireless stimulation strategies are emerging as powerful tools for guiding neuronal activity and regeneration, yet most existing systems rely on rigid, inorganic materials that raise concerns regarding long-term biocompatibility and sustainability. Cellulose nanofibrils (CNF) are renewable and intrinsically piezoelectric, offering a fully organic alternative for ultrasound-driven neuromodulation. Here, we investigate phosphorylated cellulose nanofibrils (pCNF) as ultrasound-responsive piezoelectric interfaces for neuronal stimulation, including mechanistic interrogation via pharmacological inhibition assays. Phosphorylation enhances surface charge density and promotes fibril individualization and dispersion while preserving the crystalline structure and intrinsic piezoelectricity of cellulose. Nanoscale electromechanical activity was confirmed by piezoresponse force microscopy, and ultrasound stimulation generated intensity-dependent electrical outputs at the macroscopic level. pCNF exhibited excellent cytocompatibility and formed a tight interface with neuronal cells. Functionally, pCNF significantly amplified ultrasound-induced cellular responses, including reactive oxygen species production in SH-SY5Y cells and robust calcium transients in primary dorsal root ganglion neurons. Pharmacological inhibition studies revealed that these ultrasound-induced responses arise from a multimodal mechanism involving voltage-gated excitability, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated intracellular Ca²⁺ release, and redox-sensitive processes. Together, these results establish phosphorylated cellulose nanofibrils as a sustainable, fully organic platform for wireless neuromodulation. By combining material renewability, mechanical compliance, and ultrasound-driven piezoelectricity, pCNF provides a foundation for organic nanobioelectronic interfaces and future ultrasound-responsive scaffolds for neural regeneration.

High-precision monitoring for subsurface quasi-static processes in landslide and groundwater level via solid-liquid contact electrification
abstract: High-precision monitoring for the subsurface quasi-static process is crucial for early warning of geological hazards and hydrological monitoring. Solid-liquid contact electrification (SLCE) shows great potential for monitoring subsurface quasi-static processes by offering a wear-free operation and high sensitivity to tiny deformations velocity through nearly perfect conformal contact. This work proposes a quasi-static process monitoring sensor (QSensor) based on the SLCE for monitoring subsurface tiny deformation during the landslide process and fluctuation of groundwater level. By directly converting deformation velocity into current and optimizing the surface charge density through a double electric layer, the QSensor achieves a highly linear current-velocity response with a sensitivity of 0.4454 pA (mm•h−1)−1. The quasi-static processes monitoring system based on the QSensor combines homemade signal conditioning circuits and time-integration algorithms to accurately reconstruct transient velocity and cumulative displacement from picoampere-level signals, which exhibits an excellent linear response (R2 = 0.999), an ultra-low velocity detection threshold of 2.261 mm•h-1, and a displacement resolution of 3.14 μm. Integrated with a LoRa-WiFi wireless network, the system enables remote, real-time dual-threshold landslide early warning and groundwater level monitoring. This study provides a simple, feasible, and novel strategy for geological disaster early warning and hydrological monitoring.

abstract: Carbon materials are pivotal for high-power sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, sluggish ion diffusion and interfacial instability impede the simultaneous achievement of fast-charging and long-cycling performance. Herein, we report a two-dimensional (2D) reduced graphene oxide@hard carbon (rGO@HC) heterostructure that enables rapid and durable sodium storage via synergistic structural and interfacial engineering. The heterostructure integrates the high conductivity of rGO, the expanded interlayer spacing of HC coating, and abundant mesoporous channels of rGO@HC to achieve fast Na+ storage and release. Meanwhile, the structurally robust rGO scaffold and crystalline HC surface bearing active sites synergistically ensures superior structural and interfacial stability. This unique structure realizes a surface-dominant pseudocapacitive adsorption-intercalation mechanism with a capacitive contribution up to 97.2%, and thus ultrafast sodium-ion reaction kinetics. Furthermore, a thin, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase forms and self-optimizes during cycling via progressive inorganic enrichment, effectively preserving interfacial stability over prolonged cycling. Consequently, rGO@HC anode delivers 102 mAh g−1 at an ultrahigh current density of 70 A g−1 and achieves 83.2% capacity retention after 70,000 cycles at 2 A g−1. This work offers a compelling strategy for designing robust carbon-based anodes that concurrently addresses the rate capability and cyclability challenges of durable high-power SIBs.

A multiphysics model for triboelectric nanogenerator design with explicit surface roughness representation
abstract: The design of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) for efficient energy harvesting requires predictive models that capture the interplay between surface roughness, real contact area, and electrostatic behaviour across diverse tribolayer materials and roughness levels. To address this demand, this paper presents a multiphysics finite element framework that couples mechanical contact analysis with electrostatic simulations, using exact surface roughness representations rather than idealised statistical approximations. Compared with optical interference microscopy measurements, the framework predicts the real contact area ratio more accurately than analytical models. The proposed approach captures the electrostatic behaviour by scaling the TENG surface charge density with the real contact area ratio between the rough tribolayers, computed for a given mechanical load. This method improves agreement with experiments on open-circuit voltage, capacitance and short-circuit current compared with the approximate analytical models. To represent the TENG circuit, a time-dependent ordinary differential equation is integrated, enabling evaluation of electrical responses under varying load conditions and elucidating the roles of surface roughness, mechanical load, contact–separation frequency, and resistive load. The framework provides a robust, scalable tool for performance optimisation across dielectric materials, mechanical behaviours, and operating conditions and is readily extendable to other surface-dependent energy-harvesting devices.

title: Organic solvent-assisted pore structure modulation in porous carbons for superior energy storage performance in supercapacitors
abstract: Structural flexibility is well known for MOFs and zeolites, but has seldom been observed in high-surface-area porous carbons due to the rigidity of C-C bonds. Here, a novel approach based on organic solvent-induced restructuring is reported to tune the pore hierarchy and enhance structural flexibility in porous carbons derived from waste biomass. The strategy involves adsorbing n-heptane into porous carbon at room temperature, thereby facilitating realignment of the carbon layers, improving pore hierarchy, and generating short-range graphitic domains. The restructuring of pore architecture and appearance of short-range graphitic domains, along with high surface area, led to a significant increase of 39.4 % in specific capacitance (354 F g-1/0.5 A g-1) as compared to bare porous carbon (254 F g-1/0.5 A g-1). High energy and power densities of 6 Wh kg-1/10 A g-1, and 13,500 W kg-1/10 A g-1, along with a specific capacitance of 105.22 F g-1/0.5 A g-1 are achieved for a two-electrode supercapacitor. DFT calculations provided insights into an improved pore structure and solvent-induced modulation of the electronic structure, enhancing ion transport and charge storage. The presented solvent-induced restructuring approach is innovative and low-cost, facilitating porous carbons to be more flexible and thus better utilized in electrochemical applications.

Vapor-compatible molecular passivation of thermally evaporated lead-free perovskites for indoor photovoltaics
abstract: Tin-based halide perovskites (THPs) have emerged as promising lead-free light absorbers for indoor photovoltaics (IPVs). However, surface-defect-mediated recombination and Sn 2+ oxidation remain major limitations, especially in vapor-based sequential deposition of perovskite films that requires solid-state conversion and careful control in stoichiometry. Herein, we address this challenge using a surface passivation strategy via thermal evaporation to modulate interfacial defects of THP thin films. We found that thermally evaporated 1,3-propanediammonium iodide (PDAI 2 ) on the perovskite surface significantly reduces Sn 2+ oxidation and compensates halide-deficient surface sites, thereby suppressing trap-assisted recombination and improving the band alignment at the electron-contact interface. Consequently, the best-performing devices based on the optimized films can achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.36% under 1000 lux indoor light illumination. Under AM 1.5 G illumination, an open-circuit voltage ( V oc ) of 0.85 V is also obtained, which is higher than those of the previous reports using thermally evaporated THP. This work highlights the importance of surface defect passivation for improving the device performance and provides insight into a scalable pathway for lead-free perovskites in efficient IPV applications.

A flexible super-resolution tactile sensing system based on sparse-electrode TENG and deep-learning decoding
abstract: Flexible tactile sensing is essential for robotic contact detection and tactile interaction, offering a promising route for achieving intelligent human–machine interfaces and adaptive robotic systems. However, the practical application of flexible tactile sensing remains constrained by an inherent trade-off between spatial resolution and hardware complexity: high-density electrode arrays provide fine spatial information, but require a large amount of interconnection and complex readout hardware, while sparse electrode architectures reduce hardware complexity but are limited by their coarse native spatial resolution. Herein, we propose a flexible super-resolution tactile sensing system based on a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG), integrating a four-quadrant sparse-electrode architecture with deep-learning-based signal decoding. Notably, the TENG device in the sensing system maintains stable output under water film, oil film and salt spray conditions as well as after 8,000 loading cycles. Thanks to the overlapping receptive fields formed by the silicone elastomeric medium, a single contact can simultaneously generate differentiated responses across the four channels, facilitating decoding of contact location and orientation beyond the native electrode granularity. Using a gated recurrent unit (GRU) and one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) model, the system can distinguish 24 contact angles with an accuracy rate of 99.6% and identify 96.3% accuracy with a root mean square error of 0.16 cm in recognizing 81 spatial positions. Furthermore, the system enables dual-point discrimination and continuous trajectory reconstruction, and is deployed on a robotic manipulator for tactile visualization and motion control based on pressing patterns, validating its applicability and versatility. This work provides a hardware-efficient strategy for high-resolution flexible tactile sensing, and offers new insights for developing low-complexity, conformal adherable intelligent tactile interfaces for robotic systems.

title: Anisotropic bonding regulation enables reversible oxygen redox in entropy-stabilized layered oxide cathodes
abstract: Achieving stable oxygen redox in O3-type sodium layered oxide cathodes is crucial for improving energy density, but it is often limited by transition-metal migration, lattice distortion, and oxygen redox instability at high voltage. Here, we report a Li/Ti co-doping strategy that combines configurational entropy stabilization with Ti-mediated local coordination regulation in NaNi0.2Fe0.4Mn0.4O2. The increased configurational entropy reinforces the layered framework and suppresses harmful structural evolution. Li incorporation generates localized Na–O–Li configurations that activate non-bonding O 2p states and provide additional high-voltage charge compensation. More importantly, Ti plays a dual role in stabilizing the oxygen environment. The empty eg orbitals of Ti4+ form strong Ti–O σ bonding to directly anchor oxygen, while Ti-induced local coordination changes weaken excessive out-of-plane Mn t2g–O 2pz π interaction and reinforce in-plane Mn–O σ bonding. This cooperative bonding regulation stabilizes activated oxygen states, reduces c-axis fluctuation, and suppresses OP2 phase transition during cycling. As a result, the optimized cathode delivers 91.2% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 5 C in 2.0–4.0 V and 86.4% retention after 200 cycles at 1 C in 2.0–4.1 V. This work highlights the importance of Ti-mediated oxygen coordination regulation for stabilizing oxygen redox in entropy-stabilized layered oxide cathodes.

Cost-effective methodology for electrical characterization and interconnection analysis of triboelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a promising solution for powering self-sustained systems such as wearable electronics, IoT devices, and autonomous sensors. However, the practical integration of TENGs into real-world systems remains constrained by the lack of accessible and standardized methodologies for accurate electrical characterization. This paper presents a cost-effective, broadly applicable framework for extracting key electrical parameters of TENGs such as open-circuit voltage, internal resistance, and capacitance, without relying on high-cost instrumentation. The methodology is experimentally validated through both standalone and interconnected TENG configurations (series and parallel), demonstrating excellent agreement with high-precision reference instruments. Detailed analysis of impedance matching and power transfer efficiency underscores the method’s suitability for optimizing circuit design and power management in diverse deployment scenarios. This work not only bridges the gap between high-precision diagnostics and low-resource research environments but also provides critical insights into maximizing the performance and scalability of TENG-based energy harvesting systems.
