Asymmetric interface engineering boosts acidic oxygen evolution activity and stability of cobalt oxide
abstract: The acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is fundamentally constrained by an activity–stability trade-off: while adsorbate evolution mechanisms (AEM) suffer from sluggish kinetics, lattice oxygen mechanisms (LOM) improve reaction rates but often lead to irreversible metal loss and poor stability. Here, we introduce an asymmetric interface strategy that enables a synergistic AEM–LOM pathway. In this design, controlled lattice oxygen participation lowers the overpotential, while carbon within the asymmetric interface acts as an electron donor to stabilize high-valence metal and suppress its dissolution—thereby enhancing catalytic stability. Using carbon-coated spinel (Co3O4@C) as a model system, we show that the asymmetric Co3O4|C interface significantly enhances acidic OER performance, achieving overpotentials of 289 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and 368 mV at 100 mA cm−2. Moreover, the catalyst sustains operation for 240 h at 10 mA cm−2 with only a 45 mV increase in overpotential. Operando spectroscopic studies directly demonstrate that the asymmetric interface promotes a more stable Co valence state and more reversible Co redox behavior, while suppressing structural disorder. Multiple in situ characterizations confirm that the asymmetric interface drives a synergistic AEM–LOM catalytic mechanism. Complementary theoretical calculations further reveal that upon oxygen vacancy formation at the asymmetric interface, Co3O4@C energetically favors adsorbate-mediated O–O coupling over direct lattice oxygen involvement. This work establishes the asymmetric interface-enabled synergistic AEM–LOM pathway as a general mechanistic framework for the rational design of stable and efficient acidic OER catalysts.

Cation-anion co-doping engineering enables octahedral reconstruction to suppress structural distortion in P′2-type Mn-rich layered oxide cathodes
abstract: P′2-Na0.67MnO2 (NMO) Mn-rich layered oxides are promising cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries owing to their high capacity and cost-effectiveness. However, their practical application is limited by rapid capacity fading caused by Jahn-Teller distortion and irreversible structural evolution during cycling. Herein, a cation-anion co-doping strategy is employed to synthesize P′2-Na0.67Sn0.03Mn0.97O1.94F0.06 (NSMOF). The synergistic incorporation of Sn4+ and F− reconstructs the transition-metal (TM) octahedra and regulates the local electronic structure, effectively alleviating structural distortion. Consequently, Mn–O bond anisotropy is reduced, relieving lattice stress and thereby suppressing metal dissolution and crack formation. In addition, Sn4+ inhibits Na+/vacancy ordering and mitigates phase transitions associated with Na+ (de)intercalation. Meanwhile, highly electronegative F− enhances high-voltage lattice oxygen redox activity while reducing irreversible oxygen loss during cycling. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, NSMOF delivers a high discharge capacity of 197 mAh g−1 at 20 mA g−1 and retains 84.2% of its initial capacity after 300 cycles at 1 A g−1. This work demonstrates that TM-octahedral reconstruction through cation–anion co-doping is an effective strategy for simultaneously stabilizing the structure and activating oxygen redox, providing insights into the design of high-capacity and durable Mn-rich layered oxide cathodes for sodium-ion batteries.

abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators have reshaped the development of self-powered sensing systems, yet their translation into soft robotic and wearable interfaces remains limited by surface contamination, unstable interfacial contact, and insufficient multifunctionality. Here, we report a transparent, self-cleaning triboelectric nanogenerator electronic skin based on colloidal-lithography-derived hierarchical polydimethylsiloxane and sequential O 2 /SF 6 plasma engineering. This plasma-engineering strategy couples oxidation-driven activation and fluorination-driven passivation to produce nanoscale-roughened micropillared polydimethylsiloxane with chemically stable Si–F and C–F surface terminations. The hierarchical micro/nanostructured triboelectric nanogenerator (HMN-TENG) exhibits superhydrophobicity (~152°), self-cleaning efficiency (~91%), and a 650% increase in power density (~270 mW·m −2 ) compared with flat TENGs, maintaining stability over 10,000 cycles and retaining > 80% electrical output after contamination. Beyond performance enhancement, we establish a mechanistic framework linking plasma-induced surface chemistry, hierarchical wetting, contaminant adhesion-detachment, and triboelectric charge-transfer pathways across flat, microstructured, nanostructured, and hierarchical interfaces. Furthermore, real-time surface-area estimation is demonstrated for the first time through triboelectric voltage scaling with effective contact area. The HMN-TENG further operates as a self-powered pressure sensor with dual-regime sensitivity (0.34 V·kPa −1 at low and 0.06 V·kPa −1 at high pressure) and a limit of detection (LOD) of 2.6 kPa, enabling tactile mapping and autonomous robotic operation. This work establishes a materials design strategy for high-sensitivity, self-cleaning, and self-powered nanogenerator electronic skins through hierarchical architecture and plasma chemistry, enabling intelligent human-machine interfaces for next-generation soft robotics.

Lignin-based polyurethane coatings integrating wear resistance, anti-biofouling, and anti-corrosion performance for durable triboelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have shown great potential for harvesting low-frequency mechanical energy in marine environments, yet their practical application is severely limited by biofouling, electrochemical corrosion, and mechanical wear, which degrade interfacial properties and reduce electrical output. Here, we report a multifunctional lignin-based polydimethylsiloxane-polyurethane (lignin-PDMS-PU) coating fabricated via a decoupled stepwise urethane formation strategy. The resulting covalently crosslinked network integrates rigid lignin domains and flexible PDMS segments, achieving enhanced wear resistance, anti-biofouling and anticorrosion performance. Compared with lignin-free PDMS-PU, the optimized coating containing 15 wt% lignin (L15%) reduced the protein (BSA) adsorption by nearly 75% and markedly suppressed bacterial adhesion. During prolonged immersion in 1 M NaCl solution, L15% exhibited an initial low-frequency impedance modulus on the order of 10 11 Ω and remained above 10 9 Ω after 14 days, exceeding the commonly used excellent-protection criterion for organic coatings (>10 9 Ω). The optimized L15% coating achieved approximately 176 V and 65 μW cm⁻ 2 in solid-solid mode with negligible output degradation over 10,000 operation cycles and retained ~81% of its initial output in 4.0 mg mL⁻ 1 BSA solution in liquid-solid mode, compared with only 43% for PDMS-PU, thereby demonstrating improved resistance to protein-induced output attenuation. This work provides a sustainable multifunctional coating strategy for durable TENG systems operating under mechanically abrasive and biologically complex environments.

Machine learning-based force and activity recognition in total knee replacement using hybrid triboelectric/piezoelectric PVDF sensors
abstract: Smart orthopedic implants require sensing systems that can monitor joint loading without increasing dependence on batteries or complex implanted electronics. Here, we report an implant-integrated hybrid triboelectric-piezoelectric nanogenerator (TPNG) built from six multilayer Cu/PVDF transducers distributed across the medial and lateral compartments of a tibial-tray-inspired total knee replacement (TKR) package. Coupling triboelectric contact-separation to the piezoelectric response of the stack increases the peak-to-peak voltage, while the transducers retain 92.4% of their peak-to-peak output after approximately 350,000 gait cycles. The present study evaluates the sensors under predominantly centered axial loading, which consists of 90% of loading going through the knee joint. Using a single full-wave rectifier across all six transducers charges a 0.22 μ F capacitor to 68.1 V, corresponding to 509.9 μ J of stored energy, and drives a 168-LED array, demonstrating practical energy delivery from physiological joint loading. In addition, the machine learning algorithms are integrated for force and activity recognition. Using five independent 120-cycle recordings per activity with recording-level data separation, the CNN-BiLSTM classifier achieved 99.7% accuracy on the held-out recording across eight activities. A separate CNN-BiLSTM model further provided proof-of-concept reconstruction of an unseen patient's axial force profile from PVDF voltage alone. Together, these results establish a multifunctional PVDF-based sensing architecture that combines energy harvesting, fatigue-resistant transduction, and learned biomechanical interpretation from a single device, providing a pathway toward battery-free smart joint implants.

From recovery to qualification: Feedstock disorder and the battery-grade gap in lithium-ion battery recycling
abstract: Lithium-ion battery recycling is commonly judged by recovery efficiency, yet recovery alone does not establish whether recovered materials can re-enter battery manufacturing. This review treats qualification as the decisive challenge through two linked concepts. Feedstock disorder describes the compositional complexity, provenance uncertainty, and variation in degradation state of materials entering the recycling chain, arising from mixed chemistries, cell designs, ageing histories, pretreatment conditions, and contaminant carryover. The qualification gap is the difference between the measured state of a recovered material and the criterion declared for its intended next use, evaluated attribute by attribute at a stated process stage across composition, bulk structure, particle architecture, surface and interphase, processability, and electrochemical performance, with batch reproducibility as a cross-cutting requirement. Because inherited species act according to concentration, lattice site, chemical state, and spatial distribution, controlled incorporation may be tolerable or beneficial, whereas uncontrolled accumulation may become disqualifying. Recycling is therefore treated as a coupled qualification pipeline in which sorting, pretreatment, recovery, regeneration, and characterization each remove, transform, or pass disorder downstream. Comparative entries are classified by Feedstock Realism Level, with undocumented cases recorded as not reported, and a chemistry-specific matrix separates each measurement from the criterion or benchmark it is compared against and the stage at which that comparison is valid. Sorting, multiscale characterization, and data-driven tools are assessed for reconstructing provenance and generating evidence. Across cathode and graphite recycling, recovery and structural restoration are demonstrated more often than qualification against declared criteria, an imbalance that defines the barrier to closed-loop recycling.

title: Enhancement of the droplet triboelectric nanogenerator enabled by a vertical cutting mechanism
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have attracted considerable attention for harvesting raindrop energy, while their practical applications remain limited by the low electrical output of conventional solid–liquid triboelectric interfaces. In this study, we propose a vertical droplet-cutting triboelectric nanogenerator (VDC-TENG) that enhances electrical output through the synergistic effect of triboelectrification and electrostatic induction. By using a vertical droplet-cutting configuration, a falling droplet is cut and split into subdroplets which simultaneously enable electrostatic induction on the left-side dielectric surface and contact electrification on the right-side electrode without external pre-charging. Under the optimized operating conditions, the VDC-TENG achieves a peak short-circuit current of 16 μA and a maximum output power of 64 mW at a matched load resistance of 1 MΩ. This represents a 6.4 times increase in peak short-circuit current compared with a conventional inclined droplet-sliding triboelectric nanogenerator (IDS-TENG). An equivalent circuit model is established to elucidate the dynamic charge transfer process during droplet contact, spreading, shrinking, and detachment, revealing the mechanism underlying the enhanced electrical output. Furthermore, the effects of droplet release height, cutting ratio, droplet volume, and generation frequency on the electrical performance are systematically investigated, and the device demonstrates stable capacitor charging capability. This work provides a compact and efficient structural design strategy for enhancing the performance of liquid-solid triboelectric nanogenerators(LS-TENG), offering promising applications in raindrop energy harvesting, self-powered sensing, and distributed environmental monitoring.

Controlled phase transformation and purification of spent lead acid batteries into electronic-grade PbI2 for all-perovskite tandem solar cells
abstract: Upcycling spent lead-acid batteries into photovoltaic precursors offers a route to couple mature batteries recycling infrastructure with the growing material demand of perovskite photovoltaics. Here, we develop an upcycling strategy that converts industrial spent lead paste into electronic-grade PbI2 for all-perovskite tandem solar cells for the first time. The process transforms chemically heterogeneous PbSO4, PbO2, PbO and metallic Pb into a uniform PbO intermediate, followed by pH controlled acetic acid leaching that selectively dissolves Pb2+ while retaining major impurity components in the solid residues. Subsequent iodide precipitation yields PbI2 with a measured purity of 99.9925%. Kilogram-scale production achieves an overall Pb recovery of 95.12%, demonstrating that the reaction selectivity and product quality can be retained during scale-up. Compared with low-purity recycled PbI2, the purified product improves precursor solubility, film morphology and carrier lifetime, enabling a wide-bandgap perovskite solar cell efficiency of 20.51%. The recycled PbI2 enables all-perovskite tandem solar cells with an impressive efficiency of 28.65%. Combined life-cycle and techno-economic analyses demonstrate that this strategy offers a practical route for transforming industrial battery waste into photovoltaic materials.

Non-invasive ultra-fast experimental characterization of electrostatic nanogenerators based on a new piecewise analytical solution: Applications to droplet-based and solid-solid TENGs
abstract: This paper introduces a novel, non-invasive, and ultra-fast experimental procedure for the characterization of electrostatic energy harvesters. The method builds on a new analytical solution derived from a piecewise expansion of the generator’s effective time-varying capacitance. The formulation is general and applies to both electret-based and electret-free electrostatic nanogenerators (ENGs), providing a unified inter­pretation of their voltage and charge dynamics. Unlike the standard power output characterization, which typically relies on diodes and active circuitry that inevitably load and perturb the harvester and require long data acquisitions under periodic excitation to ensure convergence, our method extracts the intrinsic properties of the device from a short measurement of a single ENG event. The test setup is extremely simple, re­­qui­­ring only an oscilloscope and no external excitation source. This fast and non-invasive operation is particularly relevant in the current trend of device miniaturization, where ENGs become smaller and the parasitic contributions of the measurement setup grow comparable to the contribution of the device. The methodology has been validated through detailed elec­trical simulations and experimental evaluation on different triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) for water droplet energy harvesting applications (WD-TENGs), demonstrating accurate parameter extraction and reliable performance predictions. The accompanying characterization tool C-ENGiNE was used to automate and reproduce the full workflow during validation.

title: Hybrid approximate-accurate neural network using vertical NAND flash memory
abstract: We propose a hybrid approximate-accurate neural-network scheme based on commercial vertical NAND (V-NAND) flash memory, in which device-level noise characteristics are directly linked to layer-dependent inference conditions. V-NAND flash memory provides a dense and manufacturable platform for neuromorphic hardware, but its low-frequency read noise can degrade analog inference accuracy. Electrical measurements on a commercial >100-layer V-NAND device show that carrier-number fluctuation is the dominant origin of the normalized read-current noise under the measured conditions. Based on this behavior, a layer-wise read-bias (LW-VRead) scheme is used to lower the read and pass biases of noise-tolerant layers, whereas a tied-word-line (t-WL) weight representation is used to suppress normalized noise and enable finer conductance control in accuracy-critical operation. The measured device characteristics are incorporated into VGG-9/CIFAR-10, ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 and VGG-19/CIFAR-100 inference simulations. The hybrid scheme improves inference accuracy while substantially reducing synaptic read power; the VGG-9/CIFAR-10 case shows a 93.24% reduction in synaptic read power, and the ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 case shows a 47.19% reduction, relative to the corresponding conventional biasing conditions. These results place commercial V-NAND flash memory in a practical operating space between approximate and accuracy-oriented neuromorphic inference through device-circuit-algorithm co-optimization.

abstract: Advanced artificial vision systems (AVSs) require both high-fidelity spatial imaging and efficient temporal information processing to perceive static and dynamic visual information. However, integrating these two capabilities within a compact sensing platform remains challenging. Here, we develop a reconfigurable two-terminal vision sensor enabled by asymmetric defect engineering at metal contact/semiconductor interface. Essentially, by spatially introducing an amorphous-GaON (a-GaON)/GaN heterointerface into the GaN conduction channel, the sensor possesses two distinct functionalities with the capability of switching between high-gain photodetection and neuromorphic temporal encoding mode under negative or positive bias condition. This functional reconfigurability arises from bias-modulated heterointerface-trap-assisted electron injection and bulk-defect-mediated persistent photoconductivity at the two different contacts of device, respectively. Consequently, under positive bias, the device achieves high-gain photodetection with a low dark current below 1 pA, a maximum responsivity of 1.7×10 4 A/W, and a photo-to-dark current ratio of 3.3×10 10 , enabling high-contrast imaging using an 8×8 device array. Under negative bias, the device exhibits programmable photosynaptic plasticity, including paired-pulse facilitation (PPF) with a PPF index of 183%. In the end, an in-sensor reservoir computing framework is demonstrated, which encodes temporal information into reservoir states achieving 97.2% accuracy in recognizing 16 motion categories at different directions and speeds. This work establishes an asymmetric defect engineering approach at metal/semiconductor contact for integrated high-performance optical sensing and in-sensor temporal computing in the pursuit of efficient and compact AVSs of future.

Solvent-coordination-controlled separation of critical metals from spent Li-ion batteries with full solvent recovery
abstract: ABSTRACT The selective separation of Ni, Co, and Mn from spent lithium-ion batteries remains difficult because these ions often show similar solubility and coordination behaviour in conventional leaching media. Herein, we design a sequence of solvent-controlled coordination environments to amplify these otherwise subtle differences while retaining solvent regenerability. Li is first extracted in a low-water formic acid medium, where lithium formate is highly soluble but transition-metal formates are poorly soluble. The remaining Ni, Co, and Mn formates are then transferred into an anhydrous choline chloride/formic acid deep eutectic solvent (DES). In this chloride/formate medium, ligand competition differentiates the transition metals: Ni 2+ favours a mixed Cl − /HCOO − octahedral coordination structure and is retained as a low-solubility solid, whereas Co 2+ and Mn 2+ are stabilized as chloride-rich tetrahedral complexes in the DES. Ethanol addition subsequently weakens this chloride-dominated solvation environment, enabling Co/Mn precipitation, followed by pH-controlled sulfide chemistry for their separation. By progressively engineering distinct coordination environments, this strategy enables the efficient recovery of Li, Ni, Co, and Mn from NCM cathodes while maintaining complete solvent regenerability. The work demonstrates how solvent coordination design can translate intrinsic metal–ligand preferences into practical separation selectivity, establishing a general strategy for closed-loop recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries.

abstract: The photochemical instability of fullerene-based electron transport layers (ETLs), particularly [6,6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM), remains a major obstacle to the long-term stability and commercialization of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). In this work, we report the first successful integration of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) as a stand-alone ETL atop halide perovskite films by employing electrochemically exfoliated MoS2 nanoflakes dispersed in isopropanol (IPA), a solvent system benign to perovskite surfaces. MoS2-based devices exhibit comparable power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) to PCBM-based control devices (20.90% vs. 21.73%) while demonstrating unprecedented stability under intense UV exposure (λ = 365 nm, 143 mW·cm-2). MoS2-based PSCs retain over 90% of their initial PCE after 120 minutes, whereas PCBM-based devices degrade by more than 75% within 60 minutes. Mechanistic studies using photoluminescence, impedance spectroscopy and trap density analysis confirm significantly improved interfacial stability in MoS2-based devices. Moreover, flexible PSCs fabricated on PEN substrates maintain over 93% of initial performance after 1000 bending cycles at 7 mm radius, outperforming PCBM counterparts. These findings establish MoS2 as a versatile ETL which provides a chemically stable interface with mechanical robustness offering a viable pathway toward durable, flexible, and high-performance inverted PSCs.

An Injectable Wet-Adhesive Hydrogel for Wireless Ultrasound-Driven Physico-Chemical Synergistic Repair of Cavernous Nerve Injury via Piezoelectricity and Nitric Oxide Release
abstract: Neurogenic erectile dysfunction (NED) seriously affects the physical and mental health of patients, and currently there is a lack of satisfactory treatment plans. Traditional methods for peripheral nerve injury, such as nerve catheterization, are not suitable for cavernous nerves, which are small in diameter and closely attached to the prostate tissue. A tissue-friendly strategy for therapeutic factor delivery in such situations is also needed. Nitric oxide (NO) and electrical stimulation are two key factors in the repair of penile cavernous nerves; their mechanisms of action are complementary, but there is currently no strategy that can simultaneously address both to activate the repair potential of cavernous nerves following injury. Based on this, a multifunctional hydrogel system (PEG@BaTiO₃-PDA-BNN6@PEDOT:DSS) is developed in the study. The system is composed of a wet-adhesive hydrogel and incorporates NO-releasing nanogenerators. The injectability and tissue adhesion of this hydrogel allow it to be adapted to any injury site. NO-releasing nanogenerators are mechanosensitive, so that NO/microcurrent production can be precisely regulated by ultrasound to promote the repair of injured nerves. In a neural cell model, microcurrent is demonstrated to promote axon growth by activating the VGCC/Ca²⁺/CaMKII/CREB signaling pathway, while NO promotes nerve repair by activating the NO/sGC/cGMP signaling pathway. In NED rats, the hydrogel adhered to the surface of cavernous nerves by injection only. Under the synergistic effect of NO and electrical stimulation, the hydrogel system significantly promoted nerve repair and improved erectile function. Collectively, this study provides an innovative, neural-structure-friendly strategy for peripheral nerve injury repair.

From Order to Disorder: A Crystalline-Amorphous Core-Shell Structure Enables Superior Ionic Conductivity and Interfacial Stability in Halide Electrolytes
abstract: Halide solid-state electrolytes are critical for developing high-safety, high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries. However, most existing synthesis methods for halide electrolytes rely on non-equilibrium strategies, which struggle to simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity and good stability. Here, we propose a facile one-step solid-state route that constructs a highly conductive and structurally robust crystalline-amorphous core-shell heterostructure by aliovalent doping of Hf 4+ /Zr 4+ into Li 3 YCl 6 . In this heterostructure, the ordered crystalline core serves as a robust scaffold, while nanocrystallites that simultaneously promote structural integrity and ion transport are embedded within the continuous, highly conductive amorphous shell. These structural features synergistically establish a three-dimensional ion migration network with low transport barriers and high connectivity, enabling Li 2.6 Y 0.6 Hf 0.4 Cl 6 to achieve a room-temperature ionic conductivity of 1.4 mS·cm −1 , a 37-fold enhancement over the pristine phase, and an activation energy of 0.30 eV. Benefiting from its excellent interfacial stability against Li–In anode, all-solid-state batteries employing the LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 cathode operate stably without a sulfide interlayer, achieving 80.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at room temperature and 73.8% retention after 100 high-rate cycles at elevated temperature. With an additional sulfide interlayer to further optimize the interface, the cell delivers a prolonged cycle life with 87.2% capacity retention over 580 cycles. Through a straightforward solid-state doping approach, this work designs a highly conductive and structurally stable halide electrolyte, offering a new design paradigm for halide electrolytes.

title: Thickness-Driven Charge Transfer Pathways in Droplet-TENGs
abstract: Dielectric thickness is a key parameter in droplet triboelectric nanogenerators (D-TENGs). While its effect is commonly treated as a means of performance optimisation within a capacitor-based model, systematic modification of dielectric thickness reveals more fundamental insights into the general behaviour of D-TENGs. Here, we investigate the effect of dielectric thickness on a point-electrode TENG using polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) dielectrics spanning 8–727 µm. Charge and voltage were measured across eighteen dielectric thicknesses, revealing a strong dependence of electrical output on dielectric thickness, with power output increasing by more than an order of magnitude over the initial thickness range. Beyond approximately 200 µm, however, the conventional capacitor model breaks down, and voltage becomes largely independent of dielectric thickness despite its continued increase, while charge transfer approaches a plateau. This behaviour indicates a transition from a capacitance-dominated regime towards one in which the saturated charge on the dielectric surface increasingly governs the electrical response. This transition has important implications for D-TENG design, shifting the emphasis from dielectric optimisation for maximum power in the thin-dielectric regime towards practical considerations such as material consumption, device geometry and integration with wider electronic systems in the thick-dielectric regime. These findings demonstrate that dielectric thickness is not simply an optimisation parameter, but a fundamental variable governing the electrostatic behaviour and charge-transfer mechanisms of D-TENGs.

Integration of Living Microalgal Microrobots with MoSe2 Triboelectric Hydrogels for Self-Sustained Bioelectrical and Phototherapeutic Diabetic Wound Repair
abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent hypoxia, infection, oxidative stress and impaired tissue regeneration, limiting the efficacy of single-modal therapies. In this study, a self-powered biohybrid patch (RobotTriboHy) that integrates engineered living microalgae microrobots, cerium oxide (CeO 2 ) nanozymes, indocyanine green (ICG) and molybdenum diselenide (MoSe 2 )–based triboelectric hydrogels is reported to enable multimodal, light-responsive diabetic wound therapy. The trilayer patch comprises a methacrylated alginate (AlgMA) hydrogel encapsulating ICG@CeO 2 -functionalized Chlamydomonas reinhardtii , a gelatin methacryloyl/MoSe 2 triboelectric middle layer for biomechanical energy harvesting and electrical stimulation and a flexible Ecoflex outer layer. Under LED irradiation, microalgae generate oxygen to alleviate hypoxia, while CeO 2 nanozymes scavenge excess reactive oxygen species. Upon near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, ICG and MoSe 2 exert combined photothermal and photodynamic antibacterial effects. The triboelectric system converts body motion into an electrical output of up to 47.8 V, promoting fibroblast migration and angiogenesis without an external power source. In a mouse model of infected diabetic wounds, combined LED/NIR activation of RobotTriboHy markedly accelerated wound healing, with near-complete closure by Day 9, increased collagen deposition and neovascularization and enhanced macrophage polarization towards the alternatively activated, pro-reparative M2 phenotype, with no observable systemic toxicity. To our knowledge, this work presents the first integration of 2D nanomaterials and microalgae as biomaterials. It establishes a living, self-sustained therapeutic microecosystem that combines oxygen delivery, redox regulation, antibacterial action, and electrical stimulation, offering a promising strategy for advanced diabetic wound management.
